title: Runtime Warnings and Trace Options
learning_outcomes: Describe Reading warnings and explain how it relates to Runtime Warnings and Trace Options.
Demonstrate Tracing warning origins in a small Node.js example and predict the observable result.
Test a failure, boundary, lifecycle, or version-compatibility case involving Detecting deprecated API use.

content.intro: Runtime Warnings and Trace Options is part of error handling debugging and diagnostics. This lesson connects Reading warnings, Tracing warning origins, Detecting deprecated API use to a concrete Node.js example. Focus on the behavior you can observe, the assumptions the API makes, and one failure or boundary case.
content.why_it_matters: Errors, stack traces, inspector tools, warnings, and diagnostic channels help locate the root cause of runtime behavior. Reproduce the failure, capture a minimal trace, change one variable, and run regression tests afterward.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Errors, stack traces, inspector tools, warnings, and diagnostic channels help locate the root cause of runtime behavior. Preserve causes and error codes, log structured context without secrets, and use diagnostics before guessing at a fix.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety note
content_blocks.text: Teaching baseline: use a supported Node.js LTS release (Node.js 24 LTS as checked on 2026-10-13). The official releases page lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS. Some advanced APIs, flags, permission behavior, embedded SQLite capabilities, module-loader hooks, and TypeScript integration are version-sensitive; verify the exact installed runtime. The Node.js 22 runtime available in the build-check environment is used only for syntax checks. This example is for learning and static validation, not for executing untrusted learner code inside CodeLeaf.

content.task: Create or inspect a small Node.js example for Runtime Warnings and Trace Options. Include at least one listed subtopic, document the expected result, and verify a normal case plus a boundary or failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates a named lesson concept, rather than only mentioning the title.
Expected output or observable behavior is documented and reproducible.
At least one invalid, empty, timeout, resource, or failure case is handled or explained.
The solution does not put secrets in source code and does not execute untrusted code inside the production API process.
hints: Start with Reading warnings; identify the input, operation, and observable result.
Run the smallest relevant example in the selected Node.js release before adding frameworks or external services.
Test one failure or boundary case for Tracing warning origins, then explain why the outcome is expected.

common_mistakes.problem: Swallowing errors or logging credentials, tokens, personal data, or full request bodies.
common_mistakes.why: The code may pass a simple demonstration yet fail with real inputs, resource limits, timing, or runtime differences.
common_mistakes.fix: Classify errors, propagate actionable context, redact sensitive values, and record the observed failure mode.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its runtime, dependencies, input assumptions, or cleanup behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Node.js APIs and surrounding ecosystem tools have explicit version, trust, and resource boundaries.
common_mistakes.fix: State the environment and dependency assumptions, then rerun the example from a clean starting state.
